summary: Iteration 6 regression on CareFlow availability editor, doctor unavailability blocks and patient uploads. Backend: 67/67 pytest assertions pass across the new suite (39) plus all prior regression suites (28) — GET/PUT /api/availability/{doctor_id} shape (7 ordered weekdays, periods, duration, exceptions, no _id), PUT validation (overlap 400, start>=end 400, '25:00'/'9:0' 400, duration 4/0/-10/241 400, weekday>6 422), RBAC (doctor cannot PUT/POST-exception for another doctor 403, patient 403, admin can edit any, GET requires auth 401), slot regeneration immediately after PUT (07:00-08:00/30min -> ['07:00','07:30'], empty periods -> [], two periods -> sorted union), exceptions CRUD (create returns exception_id+affected, blocks every date in range, DELETE by owner/admin, 404 unknown id/doctor, invalid dates and start>end 400), block-over-confirmed-appointment flow (status -> needs_rescheduling, original date/time preserved, slot_lock released and slot rebookable, patient notification containing doctor name + date + time, appointment outside range untouched), schedule change does NOT delete existing appointments, and patient-document upload/list/status + new GET /api/patient-documents/{id}/file (own 200 byte-exact, other patient 404, doctor 403, admin 200, unauth 401, unknown 404). Frontend: doctor -> sidebar Availability -> /app/schedule renders 7 day cards, time edit / add-period / remove-period / mark-unavailable / duration all work, save shows success and values persist across reload, overlapping periods surface the backend 400 detail in schedule-message; time-off form creates a block ('Unavailability saved. N existing appointment(s) were flagged'), the block appears in the list and remove-exception-{id} deletes it; admin sees schedule-doctor-select with all 5 doctors, switching loads that doctor's schedule and admin can save it; patient /app/uploads submits multipart, shows 'Document sent to your clinic for review.', new row appears with PENDING badge, admin accept flips the patient badge to ACCEPTED (class doc-accepted). Full e2e verified in the UI: patient books 09:00 on 2026-09-02 -> doctor5 blocks that date -> patient appointment shows 'needs rescheduling' + notification 'Your appointment with Dr. Mira Kapoor on 2026-09-02 at 09:00 needs to be rescheduled' -> blocked date shows 'No appointments available on this date.' -> after the doctor removes the block the original 09:00 slot is free and rebooking succeeds. Responsive: .schedule-grid = 1 track at 375px (345px) and 390px (358.8px), 3 tracks at 1280px, zero horizontal overflow at all widths; .admin-report-grid on /app/uploads is 1 track at 375/390 and 2 tracks at 1280.

minor.issue: Row is persisted with doctor_id=null: the dict is built as {..., 'doctor_id': doctor_id, **body.model_dump()} and model_dump() re-injects the request's doctor_id (None for a doctor caller), overwriting the computed value. Result: orphaned availability rows that never affect any doctor's schedule. Also this endpoint performs NO time/duration validation (accepted start_time '99:99', end_time 'aa:bb', duration 999 with HTTP 200), unlike PUT /api/availability/{id}. Recommend deleting the legacy endpoint or routing it through the same validation and putting the computed doctor_id last.

Overlap validation is per schedule-array item, not per weekday. A payload with two entries for the same weekday (e.g. weekday 0 09:00-12:00 and weekday 0 10:00-13:00) returns 200 and stores overlapping periods. The UI cannot produce this, but the API can. Group periods by weekday before the overlap check.

duration is read from the first rule of the day only (day_rules[0]['duration']), so per-period durations cannot be represented; harmless today because PUT writes one duration per day, but it silently drops data written by the legacy POST endpoint.

ui_bugs.issue: Errors and successes share the same green success box (.booking-message). The backend 400 'Periods on the same day cannot overlap' and 'Upload failed' render in mint/green with success-green text, which reads as confirmation. An unused .form-error style already exists — switch on error state.

The doctor picker unmounts while a schedule is loading: the early returns `if(!data&&loading)` and `if(!doctorId)` render a page without schedule-doctor-select, so the control flashes out on every doctor switch/reload (caused a transient element-not-found in automation). Keep the picker mounted and show a loading state inside the grid.

integration_issues.issue: GET /api/patient-documents/{id}/file is implemented and works, but /app/uploads has no view/download link, so a patient can never re-open their own submitted document from the UI.

An appointment flagged 'needs rescheduling' has no rebook CTA on the appointment row; the patient has to work out on their own to go to 'Find a doctor'. Rebooking itself works. Also the flagged row stays in the list forever next to the new booking with no 'superseded' marker.

issues: Cards of unequal height in an auto-fill grid leave a ragged, staggered layout (Thursday/Friday/Saturday rows visually offset); consider align-items:start plus consistent min-height.
The save button sits directly under the grid with no sticky/affordance on long pages — on mobile it is far below 7 stacked day cards.

action_items: Fix legacy POST /api/availability: it stores doctor_id=null and skips all time/duration validation (or remove the endpoint entirely).
Group periods by weekday in PUT /api/availability validation so duplicate weekday entries cannot store overlapping periods.
Render error messages in schedule-message / upload-message with error styling instead of the green success box.
Keep schedule-doctor-select mounted while the schedule is loading (admin).
Add a view/download link on /app/uploads using GET /api/patient-documents/{id}/file, and a rebook CTA on 'needs rescheduling' appointments.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py returns raw mongo-mutated dicts in places; POST /api/availability was returning the insert_one-mutated dict and 500'ing with "ObjectId is not iterable" — fixed by wrapping in public(). Audit any other endpoint that returns a dict passed to insert_one.

Shell() computes the active nav class from the global window.location.pathname instead of react-router's useLocation(), so the highlight is derived from a value React does not track — use useLocation().

Availability is modelled as one document per period; the weekly PUT does delete_many + N inserts with no transaction, so a mid-write failure leaves the doctor with a partial (or empty) schedule. Consider a single document per doctor/weekday or a bulk_write.
App.js (141 dense lines) and server.py (339 dense lines) pack many statements per line; split Schedule/Uploads into their own modules for maintainability.
updated_files: /app/backend/server.py (single in-scope fix: POST /api/availability now returns public(item) to stop the ObjectId serialization 500)

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows; 4 non-blocking UI/UX issues reported

All demo doctors were restored to Mon–Fri 09:00-13:00 + 14:00-17:00 @30min, UITEST exception blocks deleted, test appointments cancelled and 3 orphan availability rows (doctor_id=null created by the legacy POST probe) removed. Leftover from earlier sessions and intentionally kept: exception ex_8b1fff6145 (demo_doctor_1, 2026-09-09, 'Personal leave') and a few TEST_/UITEST patient_documents rows (no delete endpoint exists).
test_credentials: patient@careflow.demo, patient1/patient2@careflow.demo, doctor1/doctor5@careflow.demo, admin@careflow.demo — all CareFlow123! (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md)
context_for_next_testing_agent: New suite: /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6_availability.py (run with `-n 0` for serial; pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope, do not use -p no:xdist). backend_test.py requires REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL in the environment (it does os.environ[...] without a .env fallback) — export it or the whole run aborts at collection. Helper scripts iteration6_helper.py (status/restore/block) restore all 5 demo doctors to the default weekly schedule; use them after any availability test. All three iteration-6 features (weekly editor, unavailability blocks + reschedule notifications, patient uploads) are verified working end-to-end on the public URL. Unverified areas: Google OAuth, reminder loop timing, concurrent double-booking under load.
rca_of_the_issue: Only one code defect required a fix: POST /api/availability (legacy) returned the same dict instance passed to motor's insert_one, which mutates it with an ObjectId _id; FastAPI's jsonable_encoder then raised "'ObjectId' object is not iterable", producing HTTP 500 on every successful call while the row was still persisted. Fixed by returning public(item) (strips _id). The probe additionally exposed that the same handler spreads **body.model_dump() after the computed doctor_id, so the persisted doctor_id is null for doctor callers, and that it validates nothing — both left for the developer agent as they are business-logic changes. The new-feature paths (weekly PUT validation, exception blocking, needs_rescheduling flow, patient uploads) behaved correctly in every scenario tested.
